addresses.description: Proto wireguard requires at least one address, as an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR.

auth.description: proto openvpn only. HMAC digest, such as `SHA256` (`--auth`).

auto.description: Bring this interface up at boot Reads true when unset.

broadcast.description: IPv4 broadcast address (static proto). On proto dhcp the same uci option is a flag, `broadcast_flag`.

broadcast_flag.description: Ask the DHCP server to broadcast its replies, as LuCI's "Use broadcast flag" (dhcp). Stored in uci as `broadcast`, which is an address on proto static. Unset means false.

ca.description: proto openvpn only. Absolute path of the CA certificate PEM. The handler leaves the option out when the file does not exist at ifup, so openvpn then runs as if it were unset. A write does not check that the file exists.

cert.description: proto openvpn only. Absolute path of the local certificate PEM. The handler leaves the option out when the file does not exist at ifup, so openvpn then runs as if it were unset. A write does not check that the file exists.

cert_password.description: proto openvpn only. Passphrase of the private key, which the handler writes to a file that it gives openvpn as `--askpass`. Write-only: a read gives `has_cert_password`. A null, or a write that leaves it out, keeps the stored value, an empty string removes it, and a switch to another proto removes it.

cipher.description: proto openvpn only. Data cipher for a peer that negotiates none, such as `AES-256-CBC` (`--cipher`).

client.description: proto openvpn only. Run in client mode (`--client`), which takes the options that the server pushes. Only a stored `1` or `true` reads true: netifd drops another value, and the handler then passes no flag.

client_to_client.description: proto openvpn only. Server mode: route traffic between clients inside openvpn (`--client-to-client`). Only a stored `1` or `true` reads true: netifd drops another value, and the handler then passes no flag.

clientid.description: Client identifier: DHCP option 61 on proto dhcp, a DUID on proto dhcpv6, as hex digits that colons, dashes or blanks may separate, as the proto scripts read it

config.description: proto openvpn only. Absolute path of an openvpn config file, which openvpn reads beside these options (`--config`). LuCI's raw config tab stores `/etc/openvpn/<id>/<id>_config.cfg`. The handler runs openvpn in the directory of this file, so a relative path in it resolves there. The handler leaves the option out when the file does not exist at ifup, so openvpn then runs as if it were unset. A write does not check that the file exists.

crl_verify.description: proto openvpn only. Absolute path of the certificate revocation list PEM. The handler leaves the option out when the file does not exist at ifup, so openvpn then runs as if it were unset. A write does not check that the file exists.

data_ciphers.description: proto openvpn only. Ciphers that openvpn negotiates, as one entry of names joined by colons, such as `AES-256-GCM:CHACHA20-POLY1305`. It replaces `ncp_ciphers`. The handler gives openvpn each entry as a `--data-ciphers` of its own, and openvpn keeps only the last, so a write with several entries answers 422 `conflict`. Several stored entries, which LuCI's form can write, are an error of the section, and every write answers 422 until one sends a single entry. Always an array.

defaultroute.description: Install the default route the protocol provides. Unset means true. On openvpn, openvpn-hotplug provides one each time openvpn knows a route gateway, which a `topology subnet` server always pushes, also without `redirect-gateway`. netifd then replaces the default route of wan, and when the tunnel goes down the main table keeps no IPv4 default route until wan restarts. Set false on a client that must not carry the default route.

delegate.description: Hand this interface's IPv6 prefixes on to downstream interfaces. Unset means true.

dev.description: proto openvpn only. tun or tap device name, such as `tun0`. openvpn needs a device, from this field or from `config`.

dev_type.description: proto openvpn only. `tun` or `tap`. Unset, the handler passes `--dev-type tun`. openvpn also takes `null`, a device that carries no traffic, which a read gives and a write refuses. One of (may grow): tun, tap, null.

device.description: Physical or logical L2 device this interface binds to

dh.description: proto openvpn only. Absolute path of the Diffie-Hellman parameters PEM, for server mode. The handler leaves the option out when the file does not exist at ifup, so openvpn then runs as if it were unset. A write does not check that the file exists.

disabled.description: Whether netifd ignores this interface entirely. A disabled interface is not registered at all, so it has no ubus object and its addresses and routes are not installed. A stored `1` or `true` reads true, as netifd reads it, and any other value reads false. A write stores `1` or `0`. A write that enables a wireguard interface while one of its enabled peers holds a value that makes wg refuse the whole interface keeps its commit, and answers `X-Kernel-Status: blocked`. Reads false when unset.

dns.description: DNS servers that netifd sets for this interface. On proto openvpn too, this is netifd's list and not openvpn's own `--dns`, which uapi does not model: a write stores a uci list, which the openvpn handler does not take for its `dns` option.

duplicate_cn.description: proto openvpn only. Server mode: let several clients connect with one common name (`--duplicate-cn`). Only a stored `1` or `true` reads true: netifd drops another value, and the handler then passes no flag.

float.description: proto openvpn only. Let the peer change its address or port (`--float`). Only a stored `1` or `true` reads true: netifd drops another value, and the handler then passes no flag.

group.description: proto openvpn only. Group that openvpn drops its privileges to.

id.description: Create-time only; picks the uci section name (which becomes the uapi `id` field). When omitted, the server emits a 14-char `wg_<rand>` for proto=wireguard (fits Linux IFNAMSIZ for the kernel netdev), a 15-char `vpn_<rand>` for proto=openvpn, or a 28-char ULID otherwise. Useful for LuCI parity (`lan`, `wan`, `guest`) and readable cross-references. For proto=wireguard the value must additionally fit IFNAMSIZ (15 chars max). The pattern applies to the create only: a section that LuCI or a shell named otherwise, such as `4g`, takes every other write.

ifconfig.description: proto openvpn only. Tunnel addresses: `local remote` on a point-to-point tun, `address netmask` otherwise.

ifconfig_pool.description: proto openvpn only. Server-mode address pool: `start end [netmask]`.

Each entry that a write leaves must be an address or CIDR, on a disabled peer too. A stored entry that starts with `+` or `-` marks an incremental update to wg, which adds the prefixes of the whole list to what the peer already holds instead of replacing them, and refuses the command for one marked `-`, in `wg set` as in the `wg syncconf` of an ifup. procd gives up on an instance that dies too often soon after a start, and does not start it again until the next reload or start of its service. `GET /uapi/diagnostics` lists such an instance under `stopped_instances`, and a write after which one stays down answers `X-Reload-Status: stopped`. This action runs what such a write runs once, on request.

`{name}` takes the services that uapi reloads and whose init script sets `respawn` on every instance that it starts. Another name answers 404 `not_found`, whatever the scopes of the token. `network`, `uhttpd` and `dropbear` are not in the list, because the stop acts on the whole service: a stop of `network` or `uhttpd` cuts off the request, and a stop of `dropbear` stops the instance that serves the management SSH session, so a start that fails leaves the router without SSH.

Scope: `uapi:services:rw`, or `rw` on a domain whose writes reload the service, as `dhcp:rw` for `dnsmasq`. The domains of each service: `dnsmasq` (`dhcp:rw`, `system:rw`), `lldpd` (`lldpd:rw`), `mwan3` (`mwan3:rw`), `odhcpd` (`dhcp:rw`, `network:rw`, `system:rw`), `prometheus-node-exporter-lua` (`prometheus_node_exporter_lua:rw`), `snmpd` (`snmpd:rw`), `sysntpd` (`system:rw`), `unbound` (`dhcp:rw`, `system:rw`, `unbound:rw`), `vnstat` (`vnstat:rw`). `*:rw` and `uapi:rw` pass too.

When procd gave up on no instance of the service, uapi stops and starts nothing and answers 200 with an empty `recovered`, also for a service that runs, that the operator stopped, or that the router lacks. Otherwise uapi runs `/etc/init.d/{name} stop`, waits until procd lists no instance of the service, and runs `/etc/init.d/{name} start`, with bounds of 3 s, 2 s and 5 s. The stop and the start act on the whole service, so every instance of it stops and starts again, the ones that ran included, such as the other dnsmasq instances. A start sends no SIGHUP, and procd counts the deaths of each new instance from zero. The steps take their time from `reload_budget_s`, and when it is below 10 s, uapi skips them and answers 500 `recover_failed`. A stop still running after 3 s gets no start.

The request holds the global lock shared and the lock of each package whose writes reload the service, so it answers 423 `locked` while such a write runs. Such a write, and a non-uci write, answers 423 while the request runs, 10 s at most.

200 when every instance that procd had given up on runs after the start: `recovered` names them. 500 `recover_failed` when one is still down: `stopped` names each one, and the message says why. A 200 with an `Idempotency-Key` replays for 24 h.

name.description: The init script of the service: `dnsmasq`, `lldpd`, `mwan3`, `odhcpd`, `prometheus-node-exporter-lua`, `snmpd`, `sysntpd`, `unbound`, `vnstat`.

A write refuses such a value also on a disabled SSID or in another mode
